title: Philadelphia Fed Aruoba Term Structure of Inflation Expectations, November 2026 — 2:00 p.m. ET, a full 1-month-to-10-year expected-inflation curve, five days before its quarterly cousin
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 131,096 bytes) — the Philadelphia Fed's own release calendar, whose embedded structured data enumerates all twelve 2026 ATSIX rows, every one at 2:00 p.m.: Jan 30, Feb 27, Mar 27, Apr 24, May 29, Jun 26, Jul 31, Aug 28, Sep 25, Oct 30, verbatim 'Aruoba Term Structure of Inflation Expectations | Nov 20 2026 | 2:00 p.m.', and Dec 29. TEN of the twelve are the last Friday of their month, and BOTH exceptions are holiday-driven, which corroborates the November row rather than leaving it an unexplained outlier: November's last Friday is 2026-11-27, the Thanksgiving half-day this calendar already tracks as thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27 (low, estimate), so the release moves back one week to Fri 2026-11-20; December's last Friday is 2026-12-25, Christmas Day, so that release moves forward to Tue 2026-12-29. Weekday arithmetic reproduced this session, not recalled. Filed estimate on three counts: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own data schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep, and only the calendar row was read — no ATSIX-specific release page was fetched. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25 initial-research adjacency sweep on 2026-09-09, found in the same calendar payload that dated its proposer, and five days ahead of it. Filed because it is the instrument the proposer was hoping PIES would be. The corridor's standing unanswered question — recorded in all three Philadelphia Fed ledgers on this shelf — is whether an energy shock is passing through to expected inflation, and the proposer's own measurement found that PIES answers it no better than the MBOS diffusion index does (leave-one-out MAE 1.103 vs 1.107 at a four-quarter horizon, n=29). ATSIX is a different shape of answer: a monthly TERM STRUCTURE of expected inflation from one month out to ten years, so a pass-through question that PIES can only answer at a single fixed horizon becomes a question about which part of the curve moved. It is also the highest-frequency of the four Philadelphia Fed expectations instruments — monthly against PIES's quarterly and the Livingston Survey's semiannual — which is what a corridor spanning a 12-11 funding cliff would actually want. Impact LOW and symbols [] provisionally, on the same grounds as every survey entry on this shelf and NOT on measurement: it is a model-derived research series rather than a market print, no house playbook is macro-keyed, and no tracked name carries an expectations-curve channel. Whoever writes the canonical file owns (a) re-verifying the date and the 2:00 p.m. time against an ATSIX-specific release page rather than the shared calendar row, (b) establishing whether ATSIX is a survey or a MODEL OUTPUT — the name suggests a term-structure estimate built from other data rather than fresh responses, which would change what a move in it means and is NOT settled by the calendar row, and (c) deciding whether a monthly research series earns twelve calendar rows a year or none, which is a genuine DECLINE candidate. This is a PROPOSAL and an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the proposing ledger registers no forward test that depends on it.
